prompt: Build a one-pass statistics report with IntStream summaryStatistics: summaryLine returns "count=.. min=.. max=.. sum=.. avg=.." and range returns max minus min, with both handling an empty array.
explanation: Arrays.stream(int[]).summaryStatistics() walks the array once and returns an IntSummaryStatistics carrying count, min, max, sum and average together, which is cheaper and clearer than four separate streams. String.format with Locale.US pins the decimal separator to a dot so "%.2f" always produces 81.67 rather than 81,67. The empty case needs its own branch because statistics built from no values report min = Integer.MAX_VALUE and max = Integer.MIN_VALUE.
hints: Arrays.stream(scores) gives you an IntStream; call summaryStatistics() on it once and keep the result in a local variable.
IntSummaryStatistics has getCount(), getMin(), getMax(), getSum() and getAverage() -- feed them all into a single String.format call.
Check scores.length == 0 first and return the fixed zero report; the statistics object's min/max are extreme sentinel values when it saw nothing.
